marks.gloss_en: אמר לו רבי יהושע: הואיל ואין הגשמים אלא סימן קללה בחג, למה הוא מזכיר? -- rain on the Chag is a curse, so why mention it from the first day?
אף אני לא אמרתי לשאול אלא להזכיר... בעונתו -- he mentions, he does not request (= p_lehazkir_velo_lishol)
R' Yehoshua: since rain on the Chag is nothing but a sign of curse, why should one mention it?
R' Eliezer: one mentions the might of rain from the first Festival day of the Chag
one requests rain only close to [the season of] the rains

אתיא חקר חקר מברייתו של עולם: 'ad ein cheker' of rain (Job 5:9) and 'ein cheker litvunato' of creation (Isa 40:28); of creation it is written 'girded with might' (Ps 65:7) -- so rain too is an act of might
מאי משמע? -- how do these verses imply that rain is an act of might?
אתיא חקר חקר מברייתו של עולם -- the gezera shava gs_cheker_cheker
וכתיב בתריה: ונתתי מטר ארצכם בעתו יורה ומלקוש (Deut 11:14) -- written right after 'serve Him with all your heart' = prayer, so rain belongs in prayer
דתניא: ולעבדו בכל לבבכם -- איזו היא עבודה שבלב? הוי אומר זו תפלה
[the mention of rain is] in prayer -- the din whose source the stam asks
דקתני: מזכירים גבורות גשמים בתחיית המתים... וקתני מאימתי -- the Berakhot mishnah teaches THAT one mentions, and this one teaches from WHEN
one mentions the might of rain in [the blessing of] the resurrection of the dead
דתנן: ובחג נידונין על המים -- and having taught that, he taught מאימתי
rather, the tanna came up from Rosh HaShana: having taught 'on the Chag they are judged for water', he taught 'from when does one mention the might of rain'
וליתני התם! מאי שנא דשבקיה עד הכא? -- if the tanna stands on the Berakhot mishnah, let him teach this there; why leave it until here?
the tanna stands there -- on the Berakhot mishnah, which teaches that the might of rain is mentioned
R' Yochanan: [it says 'might of rain'] because they fall with might
Rabba bar Sheila: of the creation it is written 'His discernment is beyond searching out' (Isa 40:28), and 'Who sets firm the mountains with His strength, girded with might' (Ps 65:7)
R' Yochanan: three keys are in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, that were not given over to an agent
the key of rain -- as it is written: 'the Lord will open for you His good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season' (Deut 28:12)
